business_scope.primary_industry_name: Foreign Market Feasibility Study and Regulatory Licensing Agency

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Hybrid (English Common Law, French Civil Law, and Residual Customary Law)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: International Companies Act [Cap. 191] as amended; Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Terrorism Financing Act No. 13 of 2020 as amended by the AML/CFT Amendment Act 2022; Vanuatu Financial Services Commission Act No. 7 of 2016; regulatory directives issued by the Vanuatu Financial Services Commission (VFSC) and Vanuatu Financial Intelligence Unit (VFIU).

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified true copy of the passport of each shareholder, UBO, and director
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in the country of origin or Vanuatu Commissioner for Oaths

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing or official corporate extract for each corporate shareholder or UBO entity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Home country company registry or national commercial register

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Original bankers' reference confirming the financial probity and reputation of each UBO and director
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Licensed bank or recognized financial institution

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Signed Power of Attorney and Indemnity in favor of the licensed Vanuatu registered agent
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Founding shareholder and/or ultimate beneficial owner

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all UBOs, directors, authorized signatories, and beneficial owners against the OFAC SDN List, UN Security Council Consolidated List, European Union Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, UK HM Treasury Consolidated List, and domestic Vanuatu Sanctions Designations; mandatory enhanced due diligence (EDD) for politically exposed persons, including source of wealth and source of funds verification, filing of Suspicious Activity Reports (SARs) to the Vanuatu Financial Intelligence Unit within 5 business days of suspicion, and ongoing transaction monitoring in accordance with the AML/CFT Act 2020 and VFSC risk-based supervision guidelines.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Vanuatu Financial Services Commission (VFSC) Corporate Registry
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: All corporate names must be submitted in Latin script; statutory suffixes such as 'Limited', 'Ltd', 'Corporation', or 'Corp.' are mandatory; names in non-Latin scripts require a transliteration acceptable to the Registrar; Bislama, English, and French names are permitted; each name must be distinguishable from all existing registrations and must not be offensive, deceptive, or imply an unlawful purpose.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Within 14 calendar days of rejection, the applicant must file a written notice of appeal with the Registrar of the Vanuatu Financial Services Commission, attaching the official rejection notice and a legal rebuttal submission demonstrating distinctiveness, compliance with statutory naming rules, and absence of conflict with protected tokens. The Registrar shall determine the appeal within 10 business days. If the appeal is dismissed, the applicant may either reapply under a revised distinctive name or petition the Supreme Court of Vanuatu for judicial review under the International Companies Act [Cap. 191].

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office is permissible only when supplied by a VFSC-licensed registered agent maintaining a physical office at an approved address in Port Vila. Remote management is acceptable for the consultancy, but the registered agent must retain a physical file, corporate seal, statutory register, and verified UBO records. A virtual address alone will not suffice for opening a corporate bank account without additional economic substance evidence.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low—approximately 5% annual probability for a non-licensed, low-risk management consultancy; the VFSC may increase inspection frequency where a suspicious transaction report, adverse media, or tax authority request exists.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff under the International Companies Act Name Reservation Schedule

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: International Companies Act 1992 (Act No. 33 of 1992), as amended; sections 5, 7, 9, 11 and 13
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Vanuatu Financial Services Commission (VFSC), International Companies Registry
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Memorandum and Articles of Association together with Application for Registration of an International Company (Form 1)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum paid-up capital, escrow, or capitalization requirement; at least one issued share is required
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED THAT: (1) the subscribers named in the Memorandum of Association are hereby allotted one fully paid ordinary share each in accordance with the share subscription schedule; (2) the registered office of the Company is established at the office of the licensed registered agent in Port Vila, Vanuatu, and the registered agent is appointed; (3) the individuals named in the consent forms are appointed as director and company secretary, each to serve until removed by ordinary resolution; (4) the directors are authorized to open bank accounts, engage sub-contractors, and execute all agreements necessary to commence overseas market entry consultancy services.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name Clearance and Registered Agent Retention
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: VFSC International Companies Registry via licensed Vanuatu registered agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit two preferred company names to the licensed agent; the agent confirms availability against the VFSC company register and reserves the selected name. Execute the agent engagement letter and provide identity documentation for customer due diligence.
required_dossiers: Passport copies of ultimate beneficial owners
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the proposed name is refused for resemblance or prohibited character, file alternate names immediately; no remedial fee applies.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation and Execution of Constitutional Documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed registered agent and notary public in Port Vila
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Memorandum of Association, Articles of Association, share subscription schedule, director consent, and company secretary consent. Subscribers and appointees execute the documents before a notary or witness; notarized documents are compiled for submission to VFSC.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If VFSC requests confirmation of subscriber particulars, resubmit corrected notarized signature pages within five business days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: VFSC International Companies Registry via e-portal or counter through licensed agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File Form 1 together with the executed and notarized constitution documents, and pay the statutory incorporation fee through VFSC-approved payment channels. Obtain the VFSC file reference and payment receipt.
required_dossiers: Executed Memorandum and Articles of Association
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is queried, respond to the VFSC notice by correcting omissions or paying any applicable processing surcharge; rejected filings receive a refund less administrative charges.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Certificate of Incorporation and Charter Issuance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: VFSC Office of the Registrar of International Companies
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon VFSC approval, the Registrar issues the Certificate of Incorporation and the Charter. The registered agent collects authenticated copies and records the date of incorporation in the company records.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: For clerical errors in the certificate, request a corrected certificate under section 13 of the International Companies Act; reissuance is completed within three business days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: First Board Resolution and Corporate Records Opening
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Company directors and licensed registered agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Hold the first board meeting by written resolution to adopt the share allotment, registered office, registered agent appointment, and officer appointments; open the statutory registers and minute book at the registered office.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the resolution is defective, ratify retrospectively by a further written resolution and file the corrected copy with the registered agent.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: VFSC; commercial banking institutions and payment service providers
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete VFSC annual confirmation filings through the registered agent, obtain certified corporate extracts for banking purposes, and activate the company's corporate bank and Wise B2B payment accounts using the Certificate of Incorporation, Charter, and board resolution.
required_dossiers: Board resolution for bank account opening
Proof of office address if required by financial institution
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a bank or payment provider rejects documentation, obtain notarized or apostilled corporate extracts through VFSC and the registered agent and resubmit.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable – Vanuatu International Company conducting offshore consultancy is exempt from municipal industrial licensing under the International Companies Act 1992
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not applicable – no statutory industrial or operational license required for foreign market feasibility study and regulatory licensing agency services

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Not applicable – no physical manufacturing, construction, or land-disturbing activity; office-based consultancy only
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt – office-based consultancy with no EIA obligation
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: N/A – zero industrial discharge; compliance with Port Vila municipal waste disposal and noise by-laws only

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety compliance certificate for leased office premises; occupational workplace clearance under the Vanuatu Workplace Health and Safety Act and Department of Labour; structural load inspection not required for low-density office use

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Vanuatu Financial Services Commission (VFSC) for International Company registration and statutory exemption certification; Vanuatu Revenue and Customs Service (VRCS), Ministry of Finance and Economic Management (MFEM), for VAT registration, returns, and compliance. Official self-service portal: VRCS Online Services (e-filing of VAT registrations and returns).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: An International Company (IC) incorporated under the International Companies Act [Cap 222] is statutorily exempt from all Vanuatu taxes, stamp duties, and charges; no income tax TIN is required because Vanuatu does not levy income tax. For indirect tax, the IC must register for VAT with VRCS and obtain a 9-digit VAT registration number if it makes taxable supplies to Vanuatu residents or its annual taxable turnover reaches the statutory threshold; registration is effected through the VRCS VAT registration form and online portal. An IC whose activities are confined to non-resident counterparties relies on the VFSC tax-exemption certificate in lieu of tax ID procurement.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Tax_Exempt_Zone: the International Company is exempt by force of statute from corporate income tax, withholding tax, capital gains tax, stamp duty, and all other national taxes and charges, provided it does not carry on business with Vanuatu residents, does not own land in Vanuatu, and remains within the International Companies Act [Cap 222] conditions.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Section 60 election under the International Companies Act [Cap 222]: the IC may elect to be treated as a local company, thereby waiving its statutory tax exemptions and becoming subject to the VAT Act and general Vanuatu revenue law. No check-the-box or pass-through entity election exists under Vanuatu law; OECD BEPS Action 2 hybrid mismatch election mechanisms have not been enacted domestically.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (VAT) pursuant to the Value Added Tax Act No. 12 of 1998, as amended by the VAT (Amendment) Act 2018
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: VT 10,000,000 (ten million vatu) annual taxable turnover under section 7 of the VAT Act; mandatory registration applies once the 12-month rolling turnover equals or exceeds the threshold, with voluntary registration permitted below it.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time e-invoicing, API fiscal clearance, or digital stamping mandate is currently in force. VAT-registered suppliers must issue sequentially numbered VAT tax invoices and retain them for audit inspection. VAT returns are submitted electronically through the VRCS e-filing portal. A fiscal digitalization program introducing mandatory e-invoicing remains under policy consideration but is not yet legislated.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of goods and supplies rendered for the direct benefit of non-residents are zero-rated under section 11 of the VAT Act. Overseas market-entry consultancy services are zero-rated when the recipient is a non-resident person and the services are not supplied for use or enjoyment in Vanuatu; the supplier must retain documentation evidencing the non-resident recipient, the export character of the supply, and the absence of local enjoyment.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (approved export entry filed with Vanuatu Customs under the Customs Act [Cap 121])
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill evidencing physical export of goods (where goods are exported)
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank SWIFT/telex credit advice evidencing receipt of export proceeds in vatu or foreign currency
VAT export tax invoice issued at the 0% rate in sequential invoice order
Export Service Agreement / Consultancy Contract identifying the non-resident client and the scope of services
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: VRCS may reopen assessments within three years, extended indefinitely in cases of fraud or gross negligence. Fraudulent export zero-rating or refund claims constitute an offence under section 69 of the VAT Act, punishable by a fine of up to VT 1,000,000 and/or imprisonment of up to two years, together with forfeiture of the benefit obtained. Where zero-rating is reversed on audit, the taxpayer must repay the 12.5% VAT that would have applied, with penalty tax of up to 100% of the tax evaded and monthly late-payment interest under the VAT Act and general revenue administration law.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Reserve Bank of Vanuatu (RBV) and Vanuatu Financial Services Commission (VFSC)
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Vanuatu operates an open foreign exchange market without exchange-control restrictions on current payments for a tax-exempt International Company. The Vatu is convertible on a controlled but non-domiciled basis; capital account convertibility is permitted for foreign-owned entities, but all inward remittances must pass through a licensed bank's anti-money laundering due diligence and be supported by an underlying consultancy agreement. Profit remittances and dividend payments are not subject to exchange controls or withholding taxes for an International Company, provided beneficial ownership and source-of-funds declarations are maintained.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Vanuatu does not impose statutory export proceeds surrender rules or mandatory conversion ratios under the Exchange Control Act for International Companies. Receipts from overseas market-entry consultancy services may be retained in foreign currency in permitted external accounts or converted at prevailing market rates through licensed authorized dealers, subject to bank-level KYC. No mandatory timeline applies to the repatriation of service export proceeds.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Medium. Vanuatu International Companies may onboard with Tier-1 regulated digital EMI platforms, such as Wise for Business, for outbound B2B disbursements; however, Vanuatu has no domestically regulated EMI market. The underlying legality depends on the EMI's home-country licence and compliance with Vanuatu's anti-money laundering and counter-terrorist financing framework. Several EMIs reject Vanuatu-registered International Companies due to traditional shell-company perception; this risk is mitigable with economic substance evidence, physical director profiles, audited financial statements, and clear client-settlement history. An EMI should be used as a disbursement-only clearing rail, not as a primary deposit-taking bank, because it offers no Vanuatu-denominated account or deposit-insurance protection.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Vanuatu's AML/CFT banking rules do not make customer interviews mandatory by statute, but in practice major banks require at least one director or the ultimate beneficial owner to attend a physical onboarding interview, typically at a Port Vila branch or a recognised overseas branch of the same banking group. Remote onboarding is theoretically permitted through e-KYC and certified document packages, yet banks retain absolute discretion. For a foreign-owned International Company with no domestic operations, a physical interview of the beneficial owner or an appointed professional director is strongly recommended; remote-only approval is low probability unless the applicant already maintains a substantial private-banking relationship with the institution.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Offshore structure with nominee shareholders or bearer share instruments creating a beneficial-ownership red flag.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified register of directors and shareholders under the International Companies Act; a written commercial purpose statement; sworn declarations from all nominees and beneficial owners; tax identification numbers; notarised passports and utility bills; and a professional reference letter from the VFSC-licensed registered agent.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Low-substance profile resembling a shell company: no Vanuatu physical operations, no staff, no localised service delivery.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Office-lease or registered-agent service agreement; organisational charts; executed consultancy agreements with named overseas clients; current financial statements prepared by a public accountant; board minutes approving treasury and disbursement activity; evidence of fee income; and a clear commercial correspondence trail.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inbound capital injection from a high-risk jurisdiction or a jurisdiction with weak AML enforcement.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Source-of-wealth statement; bank reference letter from the remitting bank; executed consultancy contract and invoice; registry extracts of the overseas parent; tax clearance where obtainable; and a transaction-specific AML source-of-funds declaration with documentary backup for amounts above the bank's materiality threshold.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Crypto-related or unregulated asset origin connected to the funding of the Vanuatu International Company.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Full chain-of-title documentation for cryptocurrency liquidation; exchange statements and wallet addresses; receipt of legal tender, bank confirmation of fiat off-ramp; statutory declaration of the beneficial owner; valuation report at date of conversion; and confirmation that counterparties passed enhanced due diligence.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: All inbound capital injections should be routed through a licensed Vanuatu commercial bank using SWIFT MT103 from the overseas parent or funding entity. The payment should reference the consultancy service agreement and an appropriate economic-purpose code such as consultation, management fees, or overseas market-entry services. Vanuatu does not mandate a national transaction purpose code, but the receiving bank must record the economic nature as an overseas market-entry consultancy fee and retain the underlying contract. Funds are initially credited to a Capital Escrow Account pending completion of KYC verification and beneficial-ownership confirmation; thereafter, transferred to the Operational Account for use in consultancy fee payments, local operating expenses, and outbound disbursements.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Primary clearing rails include SWIFT MT103 for fee, supplier, salary, and intercompany disbursements; Commercial Letters of Credit for documentary trade settlements in market-entry and procurement transactions; SWIFT R-charge or SHARE-charge instructions where correspondent fees need to be controlled; and the domestic Vanuatu interbank clearing system for any VUV-denominated local disbursements. Foreign-currency disbursements are normally executed in USD, AUD, NZD, or EUR through correspondent banks of ANZ, Bred, or BSP in Sydney, Auckland, Port Moresby, or Singapore.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable Vanuatu Vatu/USD outright forward contracts with a licensed onshore bank, tenors typically limited to 12 months by Reserve Bank of Vanuatu supervision
Offshore non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) on VUV with an approved international dealer, used only for economic hedging of confirmed consultancy receivables or payables
Vanuatu/USD cross-currency swaps for long-term intercompany capital and loan exposure management, not for speculative positioning
FX options and call/put structures fully covered by an underlying commercial contract, subject to bank derivative due diligence and board approval

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Return and Annual License Fee Renewal (Statement of Compliance)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Vanuatu Financial Services Commission (VFSC), Corporate Registry Division
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Anniversary of the certificate of incorporation; the licensed registered agent must submit the annual return and fee payment by the anniversary date, with a 30-calendar-day grace period before late penalties commence
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late penalty of 10% on the unpaid annual fee per month or part thereof; failure to renew within 3 months triggers a statutory strike-off warning notice; arrears beyond 6 months lead to administrative dissolution under Section 141 of the International Companies Act Cap. 222, with forfeiture of company assets to the Republic of Vanuatu

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Registered Agent Standing Confirmation and Entity Status Attestation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Licensed Registered Agent under the Registered Agents and Nominee Companies Act Cap. 226; transmitted onward to VFSC
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Executed simultaneously with the Annual Return on the statutory anniversary date; agent must file within 30 days of the anniversary
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Agent's failure to file exposes the agent to regulatory fines up to VT 500,000 (USD 4,300) per violation and suspension or revocation of the agent's VFSC license; the client company is simultaneously treated as in default and subject to strike-off

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Certificate of Good Standing / Certificate of Incumbency (banking, escrow, and counterparty due diligence trigger)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: VFSC Corporate Registry via the licensed registered agent
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On-demand application; issued within 2-3 business days; not an annual statutory filing but documentation frequently required in the annual corporate reactivation workflow
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Issuance is refused if any annual return is outstanding or a strike-off notice is pending; refusal results in frozen banking relationships, terminated escrow agreements, and withdrawal of broker or payment-rail approvals

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No compulsory audit for a standard Vanuatu International Company irrespective of revenue, assets, or shareholder count; an independent audit becomes mandatory only if (i) the entity converts to a Vanuatu resident 'paying company' under the Income Tax Act, (ii) it obtains a financial services license under the Financial Dealers Act or VFSC insurance/securities legislation, or (iii) its own articles of association impose an audit covenant accepted by shareholders
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS or any internationally recognized accounting framework (US GAAP, UK GAAP) applied on a consistent basis; the IC must maintain accounting records sufficient to accurately explain transactions and enable the financial position to be ascertained with reasonable accuracy; no financial statements are filed with VFSC and no public disclosure applies

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The licensed registered agent must refresh beneficial ownership, control structure, and politically exposed person (PEP) due diligence on an annual basis under the Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Terrorism Financing Act No. 12 of 2014; every share transfer requires an immediate update of the Register of Members and a UBO re-confirmation submitted to the agent within 14 days of the transfer; the annual renewal invoice always carries a standalone UBO certification statement to be signed by the authorized corporate officer
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (including share transfer history and beneficial ownership notes)
Register of Directors and Corporate Secretary
Minute Book (shareholder resolutions, director resolutions, and annual general meeting waivers)
Register of Charges and Encumbrances (where any mortgage or security has been created)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 700 - 1,500 (registered agent, registered office, nominee director, and compliance filing package)
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: Not applicable for the exempt IC regime; voluntary reviewed or audited financial statements for investor facilitation range from USD 3,000 to 7,000 at prevailing Vanuatu market rates

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Vanuatu imposes no corporate income tax, capital gains tax, withholding tax, or branch profits tax on an International Company. An International Company under the International Companies Act [Cap. 222] is permanently exempt from domestic income tax on worldwide income. No statutory tax holiday or preferential deduction is required; the entire corporate income tax burden is zero. Vanuatu VAT/GST applies only to qualifying local supplies of goods and services, not to offshore market-entry consultancy services rendered and received outside Vanuatu.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: No official income tax return form exists for a Vanuatu International Company. The only mandatory annual filing is the International Company Annual Registration/Renewal Statement submitted by the licensed registered agent through the Vanuatu International Companies Registry online agent portal or in paper form. The registered agent is the statutory point of filing.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The annual government renewal fee is due before the anniversary of incorporation. The annual registry confirmation/return must be filed with the Registrar within the prescribed filing window following the company’s anniversary or financial year end. No corporate income tax return, estimated tax payment, or annual tax reconciliation is required by Vanuatu.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Full legal name of the International Company, VFSC registry number, and date of incorporation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Complete through the licensed Vanuatu registered agent. No foreign tax identification number or overseas revenue declaration is required.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box B – Registered Office and Registered Agent
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Physical registered office address in Vanuatu and the name/contact details of the licensed registered agent.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The registered office must be maintained in Vanuatu at all times. Non-resident shareholders may not use a foreign address as the registered office.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Names, residential addresses, nationalities, and dates of birth of all directors.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Directors may be non-resident individuals but must be entered in the public register through the registered agent. Corporate directors are not permitted for a standard International Company.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box D – Shareholders and Share Capital
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Names, addresses, and shareholding details of each shareholder; class of shares; total issued and paid-up share capital.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident shareholding is fully permissible. No local shareholder, minimum capital, or Vatu currency subscription is required.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box E – Declaration of Continued Solvency and Compliance
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declaration by the directors or registered agent that the company has not breached the International Companies Act and is solvent.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: No profit/income details are requested. The statement is regulatory, not fiscal; false declarations carry criminal penalties.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Government renewal fee computation and payment confirmation for the upcoming registration year.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The fee is paid by the registered agent using IC funds. Non-resident beneficial owners are not required to appear before any Vanuatu tax authority.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Failure to file the annual registry return and pay the government fee triggers a statutory late-payment penalty, daily default penalties, and ultimately administrative strike-off by the Registrar after notice. Reinstatement is discretionary and conditioned on payment of all outstanding arrears, penalties, and restoration fees. A contravention of the International Companies Act may also expose the company and every knowing officer to a statutory fine of up to VT 1,000,000 and a continuing daily penalty.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Vanuatu has no comprehensive double taxation agreement network and does not impose a domestic withholding tax on outbound dividends. Consequently, no DTA relief form, tax residency certificate protocol, or reduced-withholding application exists in Vanuatu. A Vanuatu International Company can pay dividends directly to non-resident shareholders by bank wire or Wise B2B without Vanuatu tax clearance or foreign withholding. If the recipient shareholder is taxed in its home jurisdiction, that foreign jurisdiction’s unilateral foreign tax credit rules may apply; Vanuatu will not issue a tax credit or tax treaty relief certificate because no Vanuatu income tax has been suffered.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory Vanuatu withholding tax on cross-border royalties and debt interest is 0%. Payments of interest, royalties, service fees, and consulting fees by an International Company to non-residents are paid gross. There are no reduced treaty rates because Vanuatu does not currently maintain comprehensive income tax treaties with major capital-exporting jurisdictions.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Not applicable – Vanuatu imposes no corporate income tax and has no domestic transfer-pricing documentation law, no arm’s-length statutory threshold, and no Local File/Master File obligation expressed in Vatu. Foreign transfer-pricing compliance may be triggered only if the International Company has a permanent establishment or taxable presence in another country under that country’s tax law.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Vanuatu applies an economic substance framework derived from the OECD harmful tax practices standard. An International Company engaged in a relevant activity, including related-party service-centre activity, holding business, financing/leasing, headquarters, distribution, shipping, banking, insurance, fund management, or intellectual property business, must demonstrate adequate economic substance in Vanuatu. A pure overseas market-entry consultancy performed for unrelated clients from outside Vanuatu by non-resident staff generally falls outside the listed relevant activities; however, the IC must still maintain a registered office and registered agent in Vanuatu and must not falsely declare a non-relevant status if management, back-office, or advisory functions are in fact rendered to related parties. Substance evidence includes VFSC-registered premises, employees in Vanuatu, board meetings held in Vanuatu, and records of key decision-making in Vanuatu.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion Through Sham Consultancy Invoicing
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using the International Company as an invoice factory for overseas market-entry consultancy fees with no real services performed, no staff, no office, no deliverables, and false service agreements executed solely to evade foreign income tax or foreign exchange controls.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Vanuatu does not levy income tax, but the underlying fraudulent conduct is prosecutable under the Penal Code Act [Cap. 135]. False pretences, forgery, and fraudulent invoicing may result in imprisonment and fines. The VFSC may strike off the company, and tainted proceeds may be restrained and confiscated under the Proceeds of Crime Act.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and beneficial owners who knowingly sign false invoices, backdated agreements, or false statements of work are personally exposed to criminal prosecution, civil restitution orders, asset freezing, and travel bans. The corporate veil will be pierced where the IC is a mere instrumentality of fraud.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company and False Economic Substance Declaration
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Declaring in the annual return that no relevant economic substance activity is conducted while the IC actually supplies management, administrative, or advisory services to related parties, or maintaining only a mailbox address with no real management and control in Vanuatu.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: A false declaration under the International Companies Act is a criminal offence carrying a maximum fine of VT 1,000,000 plus continuing daily default penalties. Where the economic substance regulations apply, the VFSC may impose additional monetary penalties, require corrective filings, and strike off the company for persistent non-compliance.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Each director who signs a false declaration may be individually fined and disqualified. During investigation, the Supreme Court may impose a travel ban on the directors. Directors may be ordered to contribute personally to the outstanding penalties and to make restitution for losses caused by the misrepresentation.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using the International Company to receive, hold, transfer, or conceal funds known or suspected to be derived from foreign tax evasion, corruption, bribery, fraud, or organized crime; failing to conduct beneficial-ownership due diligence; processing third-party payments without any underlying commercial rationale; or converting funds into cryptocurrency to obscure origin.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Money laundering is a serious offence under the Proceeds of Crime Act. Conviction is punishable by substantial imprisonment and fines, with the laundered property itself subject to confiscation. The Financial Transactions Reporting Act also imposes regulatory monetary penalties on entities and agents that breach customer due diligence and suspicious transaction reporting rules.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors, shadow directors, and beneficial owners who control the flow of tainted funds face personal criminal liability. Courts may issue freezing orders, travel bans, and confiscation orders. Restitution can be ordered in the amount of the laundered funds, and imprisonment is available for those convicted.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using the label of overseas market-entry consultancy while actually carrying on a VFSC-regulated business, such as foreign exchange dealing, securities dealing, money transmission, payment processing, lending, fund administration, or investment advice, without the required licence under Vanuatu’s financial services licensing laws.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Unlicensed financial dealing is an offence. The VFSC may issue a cease-and-desist order, impose administrative fines, wind up the International Company, and deregister the entity. Contracts entered into in breach of the licensing regime are unenforceable, and profits derived from the unlicensed business may be disgorged.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly operate without a licence are personally liable for regulatory penalties, disgorgement, and civil claims by aggrieved counterparties. The VFSC can ban the directors from managing any Vanuatu entity, and the court may impose travel bans pending criminal proceedings.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: False Beneficial Ownership and Nominee Abuse
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Filing a registry return or beneficial-ownership statement that hides the true ultimate beneficial owner, misrepresents share capital, uses a paid nominee shareholder or director to conceal a politically exposed person, a sanctioned person, or a criminal participant, or makes a wholly fictitious statement to the Registrar.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Knowingly giving false information in a document required by the International Companies Act is a criminal offence punishable by a fine of up to VT 1,000,000 and imprisonment; the Registrar may strike off the company and report the matter to the Vanuatu Financial Intelligence Unit. Sanctions and international asset-freeze obligations may also apply if the concealed person is subject to UN or foreign sanctions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The beneficial owner cannot hide behind a nominee. Both the actual controlling person and the nominee director signing the false return are personally liable to fines, imprisonment, travel bans, and civil claims. Restitution may be ordered to the defrauded party, the Crown, or foreign authorities under mutual legal assistance.
